draft.title: Contour lines
card: A topographic map shows the shape of the land. A contour line is a line that joins places of the same height above sea level.
Every point on one contour line is at the same height. Numbers written on the lines give that height in metres.
Where contour lines are close together, the land is steep because the height changes over a short distance.
Where contour lines are far apart, the land is gentle because the height changes slowly over a long distance.
draft.remember: Close lines mean a steep slope. Wide gaps mean a gentle slope.

a.q: On a topographic map, what does a single contour line join?
opts: Places that are the same height above sea level
Places that are the same distance from the coast
Places that have the same steepness of slope
Places that have the same type of vegetation
a.why: A contour line joins points of equal height above sea level. Steepness is shown by how close the lines are to each other, not by what one line joins.
a.clue: Think about what the number on the line tells you.

b.q: Layla studies a map of a hill near Alice Springs. The contour lines are very close together on the northern side and far apart on the southern side. What does this show?
opts: The north side is steep and the south side is gentle
The north side is gentle and the south side is steep
The north side is higher than the south side
The north side is flat and the south side is a cliff
b.why: Lines close together show that height changes quickly, so the land is steep. Lines far apart show a gentle slope. The spacing shows steepness, not which side is higher.
b.clue: Close lines mean the height changes over a short distance.

a.best: Places that are the same height above sea level

b.best: The north side is steep and the south side is gentle
